edges.description: TPR variants leave global O-GlcNAc grossly unchanged in patient cells, but cells lower OGA expression, and in Drosophila the learning deficit caused by TPR variants is corrected by blocking O-GlcNAc removal. Which substrates are under-modified is not known.
Shown for R284P only; the other TPR variants process HCF1 normally.

Four TPR variants engineered into human embryonic stem cells deregulate a shared set of cell-fate and LXR/RXR signalling genes without gross changes in global O-GlcNAc, OGT or OGA, so the link does not run through a measurable change in bulk O-GlcNAc.
Shown for N567K; C921Y does not impair HCF1 cleavage.

In stem cells carrying catalytic variants, lower O-GlcNAcylation is accompanied by loss of pluripotency factors, and raised OGT-TET complex levels by Zscan4 upregulation. Which O-GlcNAc substrates convey these changes is not established.

In Drosophila, hypo-O-GlcNAcylation from a patient catalytic variant impairs neuromuscular junction synaptogenesis, and restoring O-GlcNAcylation by targeting OGA partially rescues it. The substrates involved are unknown.
The C921Y mouse, which has lowered brain O-GlcNAc, is lighter, leaner and shorter than wild-type littermates. How O-GlcNAc dyshomeostasis restricts growth is not established.
HCF1 is a transcriptional co-regulator; in N567K stem cells with reduced HCF1 cleavage, expression of the HCF1 target GABPA was raised.

Stem cells carrying patient variants show delayed or altered differentiation along the neural lineage; the transcriptional changes are the proposed route, but no study has shown which genes are responsible.
Proposed link from the stem-cell differentiation defects to the brain malformations seen in mouse models; not tested directly.
Reduced brain growth in mouse models parallels patient microcephaly.
Callosal hypoplasia in the C921Y mouse parallels the patient finding.
Cortical malformation is a proposed contributor to cognitive impairment; the C921Y mouse shows associative learning deficits alongside it.
Fly models with patient variants show habituation-learning deficits alongside synaptic defects; the link to human cognition is inferred.
Flies carrying the C921Y-equivalent allele have reduced sleep stability; sleep abnormalities are reported in a minority of patients.
Delayed neuronal differentiation of variant stem cells.
edges.limitations: Mouse embryonic stem cells, whose pluripotency network differs from human; differentiation timing in vitro is a proxy for brain development.

nodes.description: O-GlcNAc levels are set by OGT and OGA acting in feedback. Catalytic variants lower global O-GlcNAcylation in stem cells and brain. In patient lymphoblastoid cells and fibroblasts, OGA protein and mRNA fall, partly through enrichment of an OGT-containing mSin3A-HDAC1 repressor complex at the OGA promoter, which keeps bulk O-GlcNAc near normal. The compensation is imperfect and variant-specific: some models also raise OGT, and a reporter screen found that OGT-CDG variants elicit a weaker feedback response than wild-type or population variants. OGA downregulation has been proposed as a cellular diagnostic marker.

nodes.description: Hemizygous missense variants in the tetratricopeptide repeats (L254F, A259T, R284P, A319T, E339G) and an in-frame TPR deletion. They lower the thermal stability of OGT and alter TPR conformation; L254F shifts the TPR helix by up to 15 angstroms. Effects on activity are modest and substrate-dependent: all tested TPR variants still glycosylate the model substrate CKII alpha, though L254F and R284P modify a complex lysate substrate less well. Because the TPR domain selects substrates and binding partners, the variants are thought to alter a subset of OGT interactions rather than abolish activity.
